subject: CONVERT function
notes:
SUSTAINED - and this time confirmed by EXHAUSTIVE EXECUTION over the whole destination space, not by reading the guard. Citation validated (--check 15.19.3 "the destination-format shall be ANUM HEX or NAT HEX" -> OK, rule 8). `if (src == 0 && !(hex && dst is 1 or 3))` covers dst in {1, 3, 4}: I ran ALL FIVE destination shapes with an ANY source in one program - ANY ANUM, ANY NAT, ANY BYTE, ANY ALPHANUMERIC, ANY NATIONAL - and every one emits the SR8 message; ANY ANUM HEX and ANY NAT HEX are correctly accepted (Convert_AnyOverNational_ResolvesToNatStorage_2023 pins the latter at 0041). ANY in the DESTINATION position is rejected one step earlier by the pair check. The guard reads `src`, captured BEFORE the ANY->NAT storage remap that later produces `runtimeSrc`, so the remap cannot mask it. Single clause, no second half.
Test-ref audited and KEPT: the theory's CONVERT(A ANY ANUM) row can trip no other rule (confirmed from the emitted message), the assertion is Assert.False(ok) on the spec's 'shall', and the method is not a legacy/GnuCobol comparison.
Editions: 2023 only, from Annex E item 24; NOT the IntrinsicCatalog row.
